articles.title: âBadly bruisedâ: Morne Morkel reveals why Rishabh Pant did not keep as Dhruv Jurel took gloves
articles.summary: Cricket News: NEW DELHI: India bowling coach Morne Morkel has revealed that Rishabh Pant's shoulder is âbadly bruisedâ after the wicketkeeper-batter missed wicketke.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: India bowling coach Morne Morkel has revealed that Rishabh Pant's shoulder is âbadly bruisedâ after the wicketkeeper-batter missed wicketkeeping duties on Day 3 in the second Test against Sri Lanka in Colombo.Pant suffered the injury on the opening day after taking a blow to his wrist and was forced to retire hurt. He returned on Day 2 and scored a brisk 63 off 89 balls, but did not take the field after India declared their first innings at 503 for nine.Dhruv Jurel, who scored a century on the second day, continued behind the stumps on Tuesday as Pant was kept away from the rigours of wicketkeeping as a precaution.âRishabh Pantâs shoulder is badly bruised. He will be assessed overnight, we want his experience behind the stumps because he reads the game really well,â Morkel said at the post-day press conference.Morkel backs Prasidh, praises SirajPant's injury update came after India's bowlers were unable to finish off Sri Lanka on Day 3. The hosts reached 265 for eight before rain and bad light forced early stumps, with Sonal Dinusha unbeaten on 85.Morkel was particularly pleased with the character shown by Prasidh Krishna, who produced two lively spells and helped India regain momentum during the day.âShows character of Prasidh Krishnaâ¦ guy who had media and commentators on his back. As a team and management we knew about the potential, for him it was about silencing those voices. He lets go of thoughts, loves bowling, does homework and research. Massive student of the game. Has potential and talent to play all formats for a very long time.âHe also praised Mohammed Siraj for his relentless effort on a difficult surface.âSiraj is a guy you want in your team. He can bowl all day from one end with a sore body. Even today, in flat conditions. He kept running in and has been the key guy for us. Quite lucky to have him in the team. Prasidh has extra pace and bounce. We need to use him in phasesâ¦ it can be risky. The whole team is behind him and supporting him even when results don't go his way. It's my job to talk through these things and give him confidenceâ¦âIndia eye quick finish to enforce follow-onSri Lanka resumed from 8 for two but recovered through Pasindu Sooriyabandara's 80 and a series of lower-order partnerships. Dinusha then held firm for 201 minutes, adding 57 with Keshara Nuwantha and an unbeaten 35 with Lahiru Kumara.Sri Lanka still need 38 runs to avoid the follow-on after India posted 503 for nine.Morkel acknowledged the challenge posed by the home side's tail and stressed the importance of maintaining pressure after breakthroughs.âTest cricket is a grind. Tough conditions, hard conditions. The ball goes soft, it was a proper day of Test cricket. We always talk about bowling in partnerships and in pressure. Fun is to breakthrough and then how well you can start again. Follow-on will be Indiaâs first target, we want to get those wickets quickly and be brave and put them in again,â Morne Morkel said.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: First in 48 years! Sonal Dinusha joins Zaheer Abbas, Everton Weekes in rare Test feat against India
articles.summary: Cricket News: NEW DELHI: Sri Lanka's Sonal Dinusha has entered an elite group of batters after becoming only the third player to score 80 or more in each of his fir.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Sri Lanka's Sonal Dinusha has entered an elite group of batters after becoming only the third player to score 80 or more in each of his first three Test innings against India, joining West Indies great Everton Weekes and Pakistan legend Zaheer Abbas.Dinusha reached the landmark during a stubborn innings on the third day of the second Test in Colombo, remaining unbeaten on 85 as Sri Lanka finished at 265 for eight after rain and bad light forced an early close.The 25-year-old left-hander had already made 100 and 84 in his first two Test innings against India, and his latest effort made him the first batter since Abbas in 1978 to achieve the feat.Abbas had scored 176, 96 and 235 not out in his first three innings against India, while Weekes made 128, 194 and 162 in 1948. Weekes went on to score centuries in each of his first four innings against India before being dismissed for 90 in his fifth.Dinusha's remarkable start against IndiaDinusha's latest innings also gave him a third consecutive 50-plus score against India, making him only the second Sri Lankan batter and 10th overall to achieve that feat in his first three Test innings against the opposition.The only Sri Lankan to previously accomplish it was Duleep Mendis, who scored 105, 105 and 51 in his first three Test innings against India.Dinusha's performance has been particularly striking given his comfort against spin. He has scored 106 runs through sweep shots â including conventional, slog and reverse sweeps â in the ongoing series, the most by a batter against spin in a Test series since ball-by-ball data became available in 2007 for the relevant shots.Joe Root holds the overall record in the category, having scored 160 runs through sweeps against Sri Lanka in 2021. Ben Duckett has 112 against Pakistan in 2022, while Root scored 106 against India in 2021.Dinusha has taken the sweep to another level in his short Test career. Of his 284 runs against spin, 122 â or 42.95 per cent â have come through sweep shots. He has scored those runs at a remarkable strike rate of 169.44, hitting 11 fours and four sixes without being dismissed playing the shot.Dinusha frustrates India as lower order digs inIndia appeared to be closing in on Sri Lanka's innings when the hosts resumed after tea at 216 for seven. Instead, Dinusha continued to frustrate the attack for 201 minutes.He first added 57 runs with Keshara Nuwantha for the eighth wicket before putting on an unbeaten 35 with Lahiru Kumara for the ninth. Nuwantha faced 74 deliveries, while Kumara survived for 65 minutes off 50 balls.Earlier, India had claimed four wickets for 86 runs in the middle session after Sri Lanka had added 122 in the morning. Manav Suthar dismissed Dhananjaya de Silva, Ravindra Jadeja removed Pasindu Sooriyabandara for 80 and Mohammed Siraj accounted for Niroshan Dickwella.But Dinusha's resistance ensured Sri Lanka remained alive at 265 for eight, still 238 runs behind India's 503 for nine and 38 runs short of avoiding the follow-on.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: India vs Sri Lanka: The good, old grind takes centrestage in Colombo
articles.summary: Cricket News: TimesofIndia.com in Colombo: The setting during the final hour resembled that of the second day. The sky suddenly darkened, and the ground staff took .
articles.body: TimesofIndia.com in Colombo: The setting during the final hour resembled that of the second day. The sky suddenly darkened, and the ground staff took position as grey clouds began to gather over the stadium. As the end of the third day drew near and the teams walked off the field, never to return, the feeling was familiar, yet somehow different.On both days, Sri Lanka were in survival mode, but on Tuesday, they kept India on the field for the entire day. The visitors dragged themselves along with slumped shoulders as they toiled for over 80 overs and will have to pick themselves up again for what looks like more hard work to enforce the follow-on. And then put on a brave face for the win."That'll be first prize if we can get those two wickets tomorrow early," said Morkel when asked about the team's thinking regarding enforcing the follow-on."With the weather around and sometimes the time it takes with taking the covers on and off, you know, we want to try and get as many overs as possible," added India's bowling coach.India had the ideal start on a very hot morning when Prasidh Krishna removed Kamil Mishra. Between the overs, the lanky fast bowler would often go down, holding his knees and catching that extra breath, but Shubman Gill never left his ear. The captain's usage of Krishna was enough to understand his reading of the pitch and why he felt that the Karnataka bowler was going to be the key on this surface with the extra bounce. This was the same bounce the opposition pair of Lahiru Kumara and Asitha Fernando used to their advantage on the first two days.Even in short bursts, the fast bowlers found the conditions and the flat track hard work, but Krishna ran in hard to create opportunities for his captain. It wasn't a surprise that Krishna took the second wicket in the morning session. He was rewarded for his persistent and consistent planning. After seeing the passage of play where every wicket came at a premium, the day also saw a period where two wickets fell in as many minutes off deliveries that shouldn't have taken wickets.Pasindu Sooriyabandara played one Ravindra Jadeja ball back onto his own stumps, and Niroshan Dickwella edged an innocuous Mohammed Siraj delivery down the leg side to Dhruv Jurel. Within the space of three deliveries, Sri Lanka were seven down with the scoreboard reading 173, and panic would have triggered in the home dressing room. They had been sitting with their feet up at 122/3 close to Lunch.Key message is whenever we're playing Test cricket, it is a grind. As the boys walked in there, I said to them that it was a proper day of Test cricket, and this is how we're going to learn.There were plenty of oohs and aahs between those two events, but India were made to work hard. The odd ball gripped, a fair few turned, but Sri Lanka adeptly countered the challenge posed by the trio of Manav Suthar, Ravindra Jadeja and Saransh Jain. India let the game drift away with open fields in the second session and then towards the end when Sonal Dinusha frustrated the visitors with the tail.The tail came back to sting India, again, but it hurt the most on Tuesday as it didn't allow India another crack at Sri Lanka in fading light. For most of that period, the attention focused on getting rid of Lahiru, while Sonal continued his ways in a rather comfortable and open field setting. Result: They have already survived over 15 overs and look in no mood to throw their wickets away.For Morkel, it was a tough day of Test cricket, and he feels this experience will build character within the team for bigger challenges."Key message is whenever we're playing Test cricket, it is a grind. As the boys walked in there, I said to them that it was a proper day of Test cricket, and this is how we're going to learn. We always talk about bowling and partnerships. We always talk about creating pressure, you know, and this is how you learn it... when there's a partnership going, you can break it."The key is to find that breakthrough, and then how well can you start your next 10, 15 balls to the next better. And that is the young guys coming in, that is what they are going to experience and I welcome conditions and tough times like this because that's what builds character and that's how you're doing it great. So keep on rolling your best ball. That's all the role in partnerships. And find ways to be creative to maybe get us that sneaky one. We've got lucky that we have 500 on the board," said Morkel on the day India had.The equation and match situation is simple for India: Bowl out Sri Lanka as early as possible, enforce the follow-on and be ready to go hard at them again. There will be situations like the evening hour on both days, and it is up to the bowlers now to ensure they earn enough time to find those 12 wickets and seal a 2-0 series win.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: âReally hacked offâ: Carse in handcuffs leaves Root âreally disappointedâ as England face fresh scrutiny
articles.summary: Cricket News: England captain Joe Root has admitted he is âreally hacked offâ and âreally disappointedâ after another off-field incident involving an England player.
articles.body: England captain Joe Root has admitted he is âreally hacked offâ and âreally disappointedâ after another off-field incident involving an England player brought the team's drinking culture under scrutiny again.Root's comments came after fast bowler Brydon Carse was pictured outside a nightclub in the early hours of Sunday in handcuffs and surrounded by police officers. The incident has prompted an investigation by England's Cricket Regulator and reignited questions over the team's conduct away from the field.The latest episode is particularly awkward for Root, who had only recently spoken about the responsibilities that come with representing England after the team leadership scrapped a midnight curfew imposed following a string of controversial late-night incidents.âUltimately youâre grown adults,â Root had said after the curfew was removed. âYou know what it takes to play for England, you know what your responsibilities are off the field, and we need to make sure we donât find ourselves with any little situations off the field.âRoot admits frustration over repeated incidentsThe latest incident appears to have tested Root's patience.âIf Iâm being brutally honest, Iâm really hacked off. Iâm really disappointed,â Root said at a news conference on Tuesday.âItâs not the isolated incident itself,â Root added. âItâs the fact we continually keep making stupid mistakes away from the game and itâs detracting from what weâre doing on the field.âCarse has yet to publicly comment on the incident, but Root said the fast bowler was deeply remorseful.âHeâs very upset, has been very apologetic, and understands his actions.âRoot was also blunt about the wider picture surrounding England's recent off-field episodes.âI donât think it has been a very good look, the recent past, if Iâm being brutally honest,â Root said. âAt all.âFrom post-match beers to cultural resetThe scrutiny comes despite the long-standing tradition of players sharing drinks after matches. Former England captain Ben Stokes himself spoke about the importance of celebrating with teammates after England's win over New Zealand at Lord's in June.âI probably wonât be real happy and smiley,â Stokes said at the time, âuntil I get up there and share a proper beer with the boys.âBut a series of incidents has raised questions about where celebration ends and irresponsible behaviour begins.Former England captain Alastair Cook offered a blunt assessment on the Stick to Cricket podcast.âJust have some kind of brain cells amongst you, seeing whatâs just gone on,â Cook said. âSurely someone says either donât go to that place, or at 12 a.m. or 1 a.m. say, 'Letâs go and find ourselves somewhere quieter if we want to carry on.âGet the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Joe Root: Furious England captain 'hacked off' after Brydon Carse incident overshadows Pakistan victory
articles.summary: Joe Root "hacked off" by "stupid mistakes" as off-field controversy involving Brydon Carse overshadows his successful return as Test captain; watch the second England vs Pakistan Test live on Sky Sports from Thursday
articles.body:
A furious Joe Root vowed England would earn back the trust of the nation after his return as Test captain was overshadowed by the latest off-field incident to rock English cricket.

England swept Pakistan away by an innings and 103 runs inside three days at Headingley to hand Root victory on his comeback as Test captain.

Within 24 hours, video footage emerged of England fast bowler Brydon Carse being handcuffed and led away by police on Saturday night after Durham's players had gone out to celebrate their win at Derbyshire in the County Championship.

  • England without Carse for Lord's Test after nightclub incident
  • With alarm bells ringing, what's gone wrong for Pakistan cricket?
  • Not got Sky? Latest Sky Sports deals or stream no contract

Carse, who was seen talking to team-mate Matthew Potts, with former England captain Ben Stokes also pictured in the background, has subsequently been withdrawn from the squad for the second Pakistan Test at Lord's with an investigation by the Cricket Regulator underway.

"If I'm being brutally honest, I'm really hacked off," Root told a press conference. "I'm really disappointed that after last week's performance we are sat here and we're talking about something not related to it at all.

"In terms of the incident itself, obviously with the regulator, there's not a lot I can say on it. It's in their hands now.

"I've spoken to Brydon when I first found out; my first concern was for him as a person. In my time in the dressing room, you obviously develop personal relationships with players.

"I don't think I'm speaking out of turn when I say he's been very upset and has been very apologetic and understands his actions. I'm sure when he gets his chance, he will say that himself.

"It's not the isolated incident itself, it's the fact that we continually keep making stupid mistakes away from the game and it's detracting from what we're doing on the field."

The Carse incident is not the first off-field episode England have had to navigate.

White-ball captain Harry Brook was punched by a bouncer while out the evening before a one-day international in New Zealand last autumn.

An unverified video appeared to show opener Ben Duckett drunk while the team were on a mid-series break in the beach resort of Noosa during their ill-fated Ashes tour.

Stokes and fast bowler Gus Atkinson missed the second Test of the 2-1 home defeat to New Zealand earlier this summer after breaking the curfew to attend a Chelsea nightclub as they celebrated victory in the first game of the series at Lord's.

Stokes and Atkinson were cleared of violent conduct but hit with written warnings after "breaching specific contractual obligations".

'We have to earn a lot of trust back'

Asked if English cricket had an image problem, Root, who previously called for his players to "be adults" while announcing the removal of the curfew, said: "We have an opportunity going forward.

"Clearly we're not portraying ourselves as we want to. We've got an opportunity to build a culture that is very strong and we can be proud of that's player-driven.

"That's not going to happen overnight. We've had conversations about what is expected from us, what it means and takes to play for England.

"We want to create something we can be proud of, what people following us can be proud of. We want supporters to look at us and revere, not just what we do on the field but off it as well.

"Over the next little while, as leader of this team, with Stephen [Fleming], and with the group of players as well, is creating something that is just that."

Root continued: "We have a chance to build something that lives alongside what we achieved last week on the field. I thought it was a brilliant performance. The way we played was exceptional.

"We have to align that with being exceptional off the field as well and understand what that looks like and how we want to represent ourselves and our nation.

"With what we've got coming up, there are plenty of opportunities to do that. But like I say, it's not going to happen overnight, in many ways we're going to have to earn a lot of trust back.

"And something we're going to have to live and breathe consistently."

articles.title: âIncredibly emotionalâ: Anaya Bangar gets Cricket Australia nod for elite womenâs cricket, eyes WBBL
articles.summary: Cricket News: NEW DELHI: Anaya Bangar has taken a major step towards returning to competitive cricket after Cricket Australia confirmed that she will be eligible to.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Anaya Bangar has taken a major step towards returning to competitive cricket after Cricket Australia confirmed that she will be eligible to play elite womenâs cricket in the country from March 2027.Bangar, who underwent gender-affirming surgery in March, received the confirmation under Cricket Australiaâs Inclusion of Transgender and Gender Diverse Players in Elite Cricket Policy. The decision opens a pathway for her to pursue a place in the Womenâs Big Bash League (WBBL), although she stressed that eligibility does not guarantee a franchise contract.In an exclusive conversation with Bombay Times, Anaya, daughter of former India all-rounder and batting coach Sanjay Bangar, described the development as an emotional moment after fearing that her cricket career had ended following her transition.âI am now eligible to play in the Womenâs Big Bash League (WBBL) in Australia from March 2027 onwards. For me, this is incredibly emotional because there was a point when I genuinely believed I had lost cricket forever,â she told Bombay Times.âCricket has been such a fundamental part of my identity since childhood, and having to step away from the sport after my transition was one of the hardest things I experienced. So this isnât simply about being included in a womenâs league. It represents the possibility of returning to the sport I deeply love,â she said.Eligibility secured, but WBBL place must still be earnedAnaya was quick to clarify that Cricket Australiaâs decision only provides her with the opportunity to pursue elite womenâs cricket. She will still have to earn a place in a WBBL squad through her performances.âCricket Australia has allowed me to pursue elite womenâs cricket in Australia. The next challenge is to get myself into the best possible physical and competitive shape and put myself in a position to be considered by a WBBL franchise. I still have to train, compete, perform and earn that opportunity,â she said.She explained that the WBBLâs overseas-player contracting and draft system means she will have to convince a franchise of her value.âThe WBBL has an overseas-player contracting and draft system, where clubs select from the pool of available international players, like it happens in the IPL or the WPL,â Anaya said.âSo ultimately, I still have to convince a franchise that I can contribute to their team. For me, that means getting back into competitive cricket in Australian leagues, working on my batting, bowling, fielding and fitness, training consistently and demonstrating that I can perform at that level.âFrom uncertainty to a pathway in AustraliaThe development comes against the backdrop of different policies governing transgender participation in cricket.Cricket Australia has a different framework for elite domestic cricket, allowing transgender women who meet its eligibility and testosterone-related criteria to participate.Anaya said she had hoped for a clearer pathway in India but eventually chose to focus on what she could control.âWhen you grow up playing cricket competitively, the idea of potentially never being able to play again is incredibly difficult,â she said.âBut Iâve also learned that I canât build my future around waiting for somebody else to make a decision. I had to focus on what I could control â my health, my transition, my performance, the scientific evidence, and having conversations with sporting organisations.âShe added: âIâm grateful that I have a pathway in Australia, and I hope that my journey can contribute to a broader conversation about how sporting bodies can approach transgender participation with both fairness and inclusion.âCricket Australiaâs eligibility confirmation said Anayaâs determination to commence in March 2027 would not be affected by amendments to its policy. It also confirmed that she is currently eligible to participate in Premier Cricket competitions in any Australian state or territory.For Anaya, the ambition is ultimately straightforward: âI would love to reach a point where Iâm simply another cricketer competing against some of the best players in the world.âGet the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: 'People don't believe me': Ishan Kishan on his love for red-ball cricket
articles.summary: Cricket News: NEW DELHI: When Ishan Kishan walks out to bat, the image that usually comes to mind is that of a left-handed batter hitting big sixes, playing brutal .
articles.body: NEW DELHI: When Ishan Kishan walks out to bat, the image that usually comes to mind is that of a left-handed batter hitting big sixes, playing brutal pull shots and putting bowlers under pressure. Kishan is known for his aggressive style in white-ball cricket. But on Tuesday, the 28-year-old made it clear that he also loves the challenge of red-ball cricket.The East Zone captain led his team to a massive innings and 210-run win over North East Zone at the BCCI Centre of Excellence Ground 2 in Bengaluru."I enjoy red-ball [cricket] very much. I think people don't believe me when I say that smiles, but it's, I'm being very honest, I really do enjoy red-ball cricket," Kishan told Cricinfo.Kishan has played 32 ODIs and 55 T20Is for India, apart from 134 IPL matches. His last of two Test appearances came in July 2023. Despite his limited opportunities in Test cricket, his love for the red-ball format remains strong."It's always fun to be part of it because I love that challenge when, you know, yes, it's easier to bat on flat tracks and it's fun as well, but the competition which goes around in Test match[es] is some different-level thing," he said.The match against North East Zone was Kishan's 65th first-class appearance. His previous first-class game was against Baroda in the Ranji Trophy in November 2025. In the nine months between the two matches, Kishan played 59 games across international and domestic cricket, including the IPL.As someone who has played plenty of white-ball cricket, he admitted that moving back to the red ball was not easy."Situations will get tricky," he said in Bengaluru, where the Duleep Trophy is being held. "It will not be easy for us as players to just move around from white ball to red ball, red ball to white ball; change of format, change of gameplay, but that is the fun part about this game," Kishan said.He spoke about the pressure and challenges that players deal with away from the field."You need to understand, as a sportsman, life can be harsh on us. It just looks very simple, like [a] player just comes here, plays their matches, and they leave. It's not like that. They go around, they keep on thinking, there's so much going on in their head every time."But Kishan believes players cannot keep making excuses if they want to succeed."If you want to make it big," Kishan said, "you want to make it count, you can't have many excuses. But at the same time, I feel you should just think about getting better and not cry about things which you cannot control."Kishan on his four-run dismissalKishan's innings in the match lasted only four runs. He reached out for a wide ball and tried to guide it behind point before being caught behind.The wicketkeeper-batter admitted that the shot came naturally and he immediately regretted playing it."I was in the middle of the shot, and I was like 'what the heck I was trying to do!' I should know this is [a] Test [first-class] match and I need to leave a few balls. So I was thinking like that, but when you don't practice so much, especially when the red ball is there [things can happen]."Kishan explained how thinking too much about not playing a shot led him to do exactly that."Sometimes when you think about something that you don't want to do, you end up doing it. I did not want to go to the ball and just play. So I ended up doing the same thing because I was thinking like I don't want to do it. I was just attracting those thoughts, which was not meant to happen, but yeah [it happened anyway]."Anukul Roy's five-for seals a big winComing back to the match, East Zone scored 467 in their first innings and then bowled North East Zone out for 111 to enforce the follow-on. North East Zone resumed Tuesday at 7 for 0. According to Kishan, East Zone's spinners were getting turn from the pitch but not much bounce. Anukul Roy picked up a five-wicket haul as North East Zone were bowled out for 146 in 50 overs. The result gave East Zone a massive innings and 210-run victory.'We'll have to be on our toes'The 2026-27 domestic red-ball season has given Kishan a fresh start, but the long break was also visible. Despite the huge victory, Kishan was not happy with East Zone's energy on the field. He wants the team to improve when they face Central Zone in the semi-final, starting on August 30."We played after a very long time, this match, but I feel the energy was not up to the mark," Kishan said, "but it can happen in these matches."When we are going to play the next match, we'll have to be on our toes. We'll have to put effort, we [will] have to fight for each and every wicket. So, we'll look into it. We'll talk, we'll have a meeting, and we'll try and put up a good show in the next game."Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: 'A tricky one': Rahul Dravid reveals big concern over Vaibhav Sooryavanshi's Test future
articles.summary: Cricket News: NEW DELHI: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi's journey in white-ball cricket has moved at remarkable speed. At just 15, the left-handed batter has already represen.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi's journey in white-ball cricket has moved at remarkable speed. At just 15, the left-handed batter has already represented India and made his presence felt at the international level.Sooryavanshi ended the IPL 2026 season as Rajasthan Royals' highest run-scorer with 776 runs. He then produced another explosive performance, smashing 94 off 29 balls against Sri Lanka 'A' in the List A tri-series final in Colombo.He made his senior India debut against England in July and followed it up with an impressive tour of Zimbabwe. Sooryavanshi finished the series with 151 runs, the most by any batter, and was named Player of the Series.He has scored 193 runs in six T20I innings at a strike rate of 189.21.However, his progress in red-ball cricket has been slower. Sooryavanshi has played eight first-class matches and averages 17.25. He is now playing for East Zone in the Duleep Trophy as he looks to gain more experience in the longer format.'I'm not sure about that'Former India head coach Rahul Dravid, who worked with Sooryavanshi at Rajasthan Royals, believes the teenager has the talent to succeed in Test cricket. But he feels there is one major hurdle - finding enough time to play domestic red-ball cricket."With Vaibhav, you've got to be patient. He's only 15 years old, and from what I've seen of the kid, I have no doubt that, given the opportunity to practice and play domestic cricket and a couple of seasons of red-ball cricket, he will be able to hold his own in a Test match team. Whether he'll be able to break into the XI with the guys already performing, that's a different story and a tricky one," Dravid told JioHotstar.Dravid's concern is not about Sooryavanshi's ability. Instead, he is worried about whether the teenager will get enough opportunities because of his growing international commitments."Whether he'll have the time to play two full seasons of domestic cricket because he'll be so busy playing for India in the white-ball format, I'm not sure about that. So skill-wise, I think there is no problem; whether he will be able to do it because of schedules might be a bit more tricky."Eight runs with the bat, two wickets with the ballSooryavanshi had a quiet outing with the bat in East Zone's Duleep Trophy quarter-final against North East Zone. The 15-year-old scored eight runs from six deliveries before Bishworjit Konthoujam dismissed him.He quickly made up for it with the ball.The East Zone vice-captain picked up two wickets in just four deliveries, showing that he could contribute even when things did not go his way with the bat.Sooryavanshi picked up his third first-class wicket with the second delivery of the 28th over. He bowled a three-quarter-length delivery outside off stump, prompting Kishan Lyngdoh to come down the track and attack. Lyngdoh tried to hit the ball hard but failed to keep his shape and produced a leading edge towards cover. Denish Das, who was fielding as a substitute, completed the catch.Three deliveries later, Sooryavanshi struck again. This time, he bowled a good-length delivery around off stump to Imliwati Lemtur. articles.title: India vs Sri Lanka, 2nd Test Live Score: India look to wrap up Sri Lanka's innings early on Day 4 in Colombo
articles.body:
India vs Sri Lanka, 2nd Test Live Score: The tail makes India work again Sri Lanka's lower order once again proved difficult to dismiss.

With Dinusha batting in a relatively open field, India concentrated on getting rid of Lahiru Kumara. But the Sri Lankan pair continued to survive.

They managed to bat through more than 15 overs and showed little desire to throw their wickets away.

It meant India could not get another opportunity to bowl at Sri Lanka in the fading light. The lower order had once again made India pay for not finishing the innings when they had the chance.
.India vs Sri Lanka, 2nd Test Live Score: Back injury no longer a major concern for Prasidh Krishan Krishna’s rise is all the more remarkable considering the serious back injury that once threatened to derail his career.

The injury required surgery and kept him out of the game for an extended period. Now 30, however, the fast bowler looks fitter, stronger and more assured.

“He has learnt how to take care of his body and what it takes to have a long career. He understands his workload and follows the right strengthening programmes,” Senthilnathan said.

Standing 6ft 4in, Krishna’s height remains a significant asset, allowing him to extract awkward bounce.

With confidence growing, fitness concerns behind him and the backing of the team management, the Karnataka pacer increasingly looks like the strike bowler India believe he can become..India vs Sri Lanka, 2nd Test Live Score: Sonal Dinusha Sonal Dinusha is the third batter to have gone past 80 in each of his first three Test innings against India, after Zaheer Abbas (176, 96 and 235*) and Everton Weekes (128, 194, 162).

(Weekes got hundreds in each of his first four outings vs India and was dismissed for 90 in his fifth)
. A call to make - India's bowling coach Morne Morkel has not ruled out enforcing the follow-on if the opportunity presents itself, but Shubman Gill has not been particularly keen on taking that route since becoming Test captain. With the weather likely to play a part over the remaining two days, India may have to be brave with their decisions, especially with valuable WTC points up for grabs.. Time is of the essence - At 173/7, it could have all gone horribly wrong for Sri Lanka, but they have shown plenty of grit with the bat. The first task for Sonal Dinusha and Co. will be to add 39 more runs to take the follow-on out of India’s hands and, more importantly, eat up time.. Greetings, all - India dominated the first two days, but just as they did in Galle, Sri Lanka have shown that they have plenty of fight in them and will not go away quietly. There is still plenty to play for, so settle in for what promises to be another intriguing day. Reminder that play will start at 4.15 am GMT (9.45 am IST) to make up for the time lost to the weather.. ... DAY 4, SESSION 1 ....India vs Sri Lanka, 2nd Test Live Score: India let Sri Lanka off the hook India had appeared well placed to secure a sizeable lead and potentially enforce the follow-on after reducing Sri Lanka to 216/7.

However, Dinusha and the lower order displayed plenty of resolve to blunt the visitors’ bowling attack.

Earlier, Sri Lanka showed intent from the outset.

Sooriyabandara and Kamindu Mendis (32) stitched together an 87-run third-wicket partnership, helping the hosts add 122 runs while losing only two wickets in the opening session.

Sooriyabandara brought up his maiden Test fifty off 76 balls before falling to Ravindra Jadeja while attempting a late cut.
.India vs Sri Lanka, 2nd Test Live Score: Sri Lanka's batters refuse to panic Despite losing wickets, Sri Lanka did not allow India to run through their batting order.

The odd delivery gripped and several turned, but Sri Lanka's batters dealt with the threat posed by Manav Suthar, Ravindra Jadeja and Saransh Jain.

India also allowed the game to drift during parts of the second session, with open fields giving Sri Lanka's batters opportunities to survive.

The same happened late in the day when Sonal Dinusha frustrated India alongside the lower order.

.India vs Sri Lanka, 2nd Test Live Score: Dinusha leads Sri Lanka's fightback Dinusha, now the leading run-scorer of the series with 269 runs at 134.50, was closing in on a second Test century in as many matches when rain and bad light forced an early finish to the proceedings.

Together with Lahiru Kumara (8 batting), he added an unbeaten 35-run stand for the ninth wicket, after earlier sharing a crucial 57-run partnership with Keshara Nuwantha (18).

The 25-year-old has now registered three consecutive 80-plus scores in the series, underlining his credentials as a long-term solution to Sri Lanka’s batting woes in the middle order.

With Pathum Nissanka, Kusal Mendis and Dinesh Chandimal unavailable, Dinusha has shouldered responsibility admirably..India vs Sri Lanka, 2nd Test Live Score: Two wickets in three balls change the mood For much of the day, India had to work extremely hard for wickets. Then, suddenly, two came almost out of nowhere.

Pasindu Sooriyabandara played a Ravindra Jadeja delivery back onto his own stumps. Niroshan Dickwella then edged a Mohammed Siraj delivery down the leg side to wicketkeeper Dhruv Jurel.

The two wickets came within three deliveries.

Sri Lanka were suddenly seven down at 173. It was a huge change from the situation before lunch when they were comfortably placed at 122/3.
.India vs Sri Lanka, 2nd Test Live Score: The qualities that make Krishna dangerous One of Krishna’s biggest strengths today is his ability to combine steep bounce with a sharp leg-cutter and a well-disguised wobble-seam delivery.

MRF Pace Foundation chief coach M Senthilnathan feels those qualities have helped him evolve into a bowler capable of making an impact whenever India need a breakthrough.

“We always felt he had the potential to play at the highest level. Slowly, Krishna is turning into a spearhead of the Indian team and cementing his place. The most important thing is that he picks up wickets whenever he comes into the attack and breaks partnerships,” Senthilnathan said.

The coach believes regular opportunities at the international level have accelerated Krishna’s growth.

“The more fast bowlers play, the more confident they become. Now he feels that he belongs in the Indian team. The management has given him the confidence and they have seen that there is something special in him after all.”
.India vs Sri Lanka, 2nd Test Live Score: Early exposure to Australian greats In 2016, as part of the IDBI Federal Bowling Foundation, he travelled to Australia with Tushar Deshpande and other young pacers to train under Australian fast-bowling great Jeff Thomson at Cricket Australia’s Centre of Excellence in Brisbane.

Former cricket administrator Dr Makarand Waingankar believes the exposure played a significant role in Krishna’s development.

“They trained under Thomson, Greg Chappell and Michael Kasprowicz. That exposure stood Prasidh in good stead and helped improve his skills,” Waingankar told TOI.

A year later, Krishna joined the MRF Pace Foundation in Chennai, where he honed his craft under legendary Australian quick Glenn McGrath.

Over the years, McGrath and Brett Lee have both spoken highly of the Karnataka pacer, reinforcing the belief that he possessed the attributes needed to succeed at the highest level..India vs Sri Lanka, 2nd Test Live Score: Prasidh sets the tone on a tough morning India got the start they wanted on a hot morning when Prasidh Krishna dismissed Kamil Mishra.

Krishna was clearly working hard on a flat surface. Between overs, the tall fast bowler often bent down, held his knees and took a few extra breaths. But captain Shubman Gill kept talking to him and stayed close throughout his spell.

Gill's continued use of Krishna showed how highly he rated the bowler's ability to extract extra bounce from the surface. That bounce had also helped Sri Lanka's Lahiru Kumara and Asitha Fernando during the first two days.

The fast bowlers had to work hard even in short spells, but Krishna continued running in and looking for opportunities. His second wicket of the morning was a reward for his patience and consistent plans.
.India vs Sri Lanka, 2nd Test Live Score: Sri Lanka refuse to surrender Yet, Sri Lanka refused to surrender.

Aided by interruptions and determined lower-order resistance, Dinusha ensured India were left waiting for the final two wickets..India vs Sri Lanka, 2nd Test Live Score: Sri Lanka 38 runs away from follow-on; India remain in control If it’s Devdutt Padikkal and Dhruv Jurel that have emerged as India’s batting stars of the future in this series, Sonal Dinusha is making a similar statement for Sri Lanka.

The left-hander followed his scores of 100 and 84 in Galle with an unbeaten 85 (137b, 2x6) to lead a gritty fightback on a rain-hit third day of the second Test at SSC on Tuesday.

Dinusha found an able ally in fellow youngster Pasindu Sooriyabandara, who struck 80 (133b, 9x4) in only his second Test innings, as Sri Lanka frustrated India for large parts of the day before ending on 265 for eight.

The hosts still require 38 runs to avoid the follow-on after India posted 503 for nine declared, but the resistance shown by their young batting brigade has ensured they remain in the contest..India vs Sri Lanka, 2nd Test Live Score: 'He is maturing and becoming a strike bowler' Senthilnathan highlighted Krishna’s height, pace and ability to strike at crucial moments as hallmarks of a mature fast bowler.

“He has extra bounce, good speed and gets breakthroughs exactly when India want them. Those are signs that he is maturing and becoming a strike bowler.”

While India captain Shubman Gill recently described this as the best version of Krishna, his former coach believes there is still more to come.

According to Senthilnathan, Krishna is learning how to use the short ball to create pressure before finishing batters off with fuller deliveries, an important skill for a modern Test pacer.

.India vs Sri Lanka, 2nd Test Live Score: How Prasidh became Gill’s go-to man Another impressive outing by Prasidh Krishna, who returned figures of 3-47 in 14 overs on a day when Sri Lanka’s batters showed plenty of resolve before rain halted play, emerged as one of India’s biggest positives on Day Three of the second Test at SSC.

The tall pacer used the short ball effectively to dismiss Kamil Mishara and Kamindu Mendis, underlining his growing stature in India’s pace attack.

Krishna’s journey to becoming a dependable Test bowler can be traced back to two formative stints during his teenage years..India vs Sri Lanka, 2nd Test Live Score: The good, old grind takes centrestage in Colombo The final hour in Colombo brought back familiar scenes from the previous day. The sky turned dark, grey clouds gathered over the stadium and the ground staff moved into position. As the third day's play ended, the teams walked off the field, leaving behind a match that had followed a familiar pattern but with one big difference.

Sri Lanka were again fighting for survival, but this time they made India work for every wicket. The visitors spent more than 80 overs in the field and will have to return for another long spell as they look to take the final two wickets, enforce the follow-on and then chase a 2-0 series win.

"That'll be first prize if we can get those two wickets tomorrow early," said Morkel when asked about India's plans to enforce the follow-on.

"With the weather around and sometimes the time it takes with taking the covers on and off, you know, we want to try and get as many overs as possible," added India's bowling coach..India vs Sri Lanka, 2nd Test Live Score: India dominate after big first innings India declared their first innings at 503 for nine on Day 2, with Devdutt Padikkal scoring 117 and Druv Jurel remaining unbeaten on 115.

Sri Lanka's reply got off to a poor start. They were reduced to 8 for two by the close of play on Day 2 and then lost overnight batter Kamil Mishara for 19 with the total at 35.

Krishna led India's bowling attack with figures of 3-47, while Suthar finished the day with 3-83.

Sri Lanka now need 39 more runs to avoid the follow-on, with only two wickets left.

India lead the two-Test series 1-0 after beating Sri Lanka by 165 runs in the opening Test at Galle..India vs Sri Lanka, 2nd Test Live Score: Nuwantha's resistance ends Niroshan Dickwella was dismissed for a duck, leaving Sri Lanka struggling at 173 for seven.

Nuwantha then joined Dinusha and helped the hosts stretch their innings.

However, his resistance ended when he charged down the pitch against Suthar. He failed to control his shot and was caught by Saransh Jain.

.India vs Sri Lanka, 2nd Test Live Score: Sooriyabandara misses out on century
Pasindu Sooriyabandara scored a fighting 80 before Ravindra Jadeja bowled him.

The batter had looked composed despite Sri Lanka's early problems and faced 133 deliveries, hitting nine boundaries.

In the first Test in Galle, Sooriyabandara had been dismissed for a first-ball duck while appearing as a concussion substitute for Dinesh Chandimal. This time, he showed much greater confidence and played a crucial role in rebuilding Sri Lanka's innings.

Sooriyabandara added 87 runs off 126 balls with Kamindu Mendis, who scored 32.

The partnership helped Sri Lanka recover before Mendis was dismissed shortly before lunch. He hit a delivery from Krishna to Jadeja at midwicket.

.India vs Sri Lanka, 2nd Test Live Score: Suthar removes Sri Lanka captain Sri Lanka went to lunch at 130 for four but lost captain Dhananjaya de Silva soon after the break.

Just seven runs had been added to the total when Dhananjaya was dismissed for eight. He was caught at slip by KL Rahul off Suthar's bowling.

India continued to put pressure on the hosts as the Sri Lankan batting order struggled to build partnerships..India vs Sri Lanka, 2nd Test Live Score: Dinusha keeps Sri Lanka fighting Sonal Dinusha once again stood out with the bat for Sri Lanka. The No. 7 batter was unbeaten on 85 when play ended early due to rain.

Dinusha faced 137 deliveries and hit six boundaries and two sixes. His latest innings continued an impressive run that saw him score 100 and 84 in the two innings of the first Test in Galle.

He shared a 57-run partnership for the eighth wicket with Keshara Nuwantha, who made 18 off 74 balls.

Lahiru Kumara was unbeaten on eight alongside Dinusha when rain brought an early end to play..India vs Sri Lanka, 2nd Test Live Score: Hello and welcome Hello and welcome to the Live coverage of Day 4 of the second Test match between India and Sri Lanka in Colombo.

India remained firmly in control of the second Test as fast bowler Prasidh Krishna and spinner Manav Suthar picked up three wickets each to reduce Sri Lanka to 265 for eight at stumps on Day 3 on Tuesday.

India had declared their first innings at 503 for nine, leaving Sri Lanka needing another 39 runs to avoid the follow-on with only two wickets remaining.. A crucial Day 4 awaits - Still, India look set to come away with a significant lead, and with a good night’s rest and the second new ball, they will look to wrap things up quickly on Day 4. Lahiru Kumara did have a couple of moments when he ran out of patience, but got away with it. He will need to provide able support to Sonal Dinusha as the home side look to stretch the innings out and eat into the deficit. Two days remain in the Test, and whenever India get their turn to bat, they will have to plan their declaration with the weather in mind and work out how much time they need to take 10 Sri Lankan wickets. We did see the pitch showing signs of deterioration in the third session, and how it plays out remains to be seen. It will be another early start on Day 4 to make up for the time lost to rain, with the first ball scheduled for 4.15 am GMT (9.45 am IST). See you then. Cheers!. Sri Lanka keep India at bay - The story of the first couple of sessions was largely serene for Sri Lanka. Out of nowhere, India would pick up a wicket, but the hosts responded by putting together another partnership and continued to chip away at the deficit. 5 wickets fell across the two sessions, but Sri Lanka scored 208 runs in that period, with Pasindu Sooriyabandara leading the charge early on before Sonal Dinusha took over. At 173/7, India had their tails up with a double strike, and one might have feared the worst for the home side, but Dinusha fought on, with able support from the bowlers.. 11.46 am GMT (5.16 pm IST) - STUMPS, DAY 3 - That's that for the day. With no signs of the weather improving, the umpires have pulled the plug on the day. That draws the curtains on another attritional day of Test cricket. Up against it at the start of the day, 495 runs adrift with 8 wickets in hand, Sri Lanka showed plenty of grit and resolve with the bat while also taking valuable time out of the game. India did not quite start well with the ball and leaked runs at 4.2 an over in the morning session. The second session brought some semblance of control, with three wickets falling in the afternoon, but they then ran into stiff resistance from Sonal Dinusha and the bowlers.. 11.39 am GMT (5.09 pm IST) - Unfortunately, that drizzle is picking up pace now. And it looks like we are done for the day here. More and more covers are being dragged in to protect the playing area. The match officials are out, strolling across the covers with umbrellas open overhead, taking stock of the situation as the rain continues to fall.. 11.34 am GMT (5.04 pm IST) - Alas! It was looking really gloomy, and now the drizzle has arrived. And it sends the ground staff sprinting in from every corner of the field. Covers in hand, it turns into a bit of a race among them to see who gets to the middle first. And just as we speak, almost the entire ground is under blue sheets with the pitch and squares protected right away. As of now, it isn't a heavy downpour just yet, more a soft sprinkle, but the sky overhead has taken on a look straight out of Gotham City.. Game stopped due to : Rain Stoppage.India vs Sri Lanka, 2nd Test Live Score: 265/8 (83.4 overs) 83.4: Ravindra Jadeja to Lahiru Kumara, Fuller and around the leg stump. Kumara gets down on a knee and has a big slog across the line. It spins past the blade and crashes into the back thigh. The ball lands well beyond the line of the leg pole..India vs Sri Lanka, 2nd Test Live Score: 265/8 (83.3 overs) 83.3: Ravindra Jadeja to Lahiru Kumara, From around the wicket, not all that short, spinning back in with bounce. Kumara misses out on the flick and gets hit on the pads..India vs Sri Lanka, 2nd Test Live Score: 265/8 (83.2 overs) 83.2: Ravindra Jadeja to Sonal Dinusha, Floated up, on middle. Sonal uses his feet and knocks it to long on for a run..India vs Sri Lanka, 2nd Test Live Score: 264/8 (83.1 overs) 83.1: Ravindra Jadeja to Sonal Dinusha, A hint of spin, on a good length, on middle. Sonal stabs it down from the crease.. The on-field umpires have conveyed to Gill that the light is constantly fading and it is not safe enough for the seamers to continue. Hence, Ravindra Jadeja is back into the attack, replacing Prasidh Krishna. There are still 18 overs left in the day on paper, but with conditions worsening, getting through all of them looks like a stretch..India vs Sri Lanka, 2nd Test Live Score: 264/8 (82.6 overs) 82.6: Saransh Jain to Lahiru Kumara, Offers flight, fuller and on middle. Lahiru leans forward to defend..India vs Sri Lanka, 2nd Test Live Score: 264/8 (82.5 overs) 82.5: Saransh Jain to Lahiru Kumara, Short and darted in, on middle. Kumara stays back to block it out..India vs Sri Lanka, 2nd Test Live Score: 264/8 (82.4 overs) 82.4: Saransh Jain to Sonal Dinusha, Too straight, angled in at the pads. Dinusha tries to tickle it away. A leg bye is taken as the ball goes off the pads down to deep fine leg..India vs Sri Lanka, 2nd Test Live Score: 263/8 (82.3 overs) 82.3: Saransh Jain to Sonal Dinusha, Flatter and shorter, on middle. Sonal hangs back to stab it down..India vs Sri Lanka, 2nd Test Live Score: 263/8 (82.2 overs) 82.2: Saransh Jain to Sonal Dinusha, Full and drifting in, on middle, kept out off the front foot..India vs Sri Lanka, 2nd Test Live Score: 263/8 (82.1 overs) 82.1: Saransh Jain to Sonal Dinusha, A ripper by Jain. Drifting in from around the wicket, full and landing on middle before spinning away with bounce. Dinusha lunges for the block but is beaten past the outside edge.. The light meter is out as umpire Ahsan Raza walks to have a chat with the other umpire, Sharfuddoula Saikat. But for now, the reading suggests it's still fine to carry on. Sonal Dinusha, meanwhile, pulls up stiff again and calls for the physio once more. Overhead, the skies have turned considerably darker, and the members of the ground staff are already jogging toward the covers stacked along the boundary, ready to pull them out at the first sign of trouble. Live visuals now show rain falling just a couple of kilometres from the stadium, and it could well be heading this way before too long..India vs Sri Lanka, 2nd Test Live Score: 263/8 (81.6 overs) 81.6: Prasidh Krishna to Lahiru Kumara, Nearly dragged it on. Low full toss, outside off. Kumara is perhaps expecting a short ball with a short leg in place. He hangs deep in the crease and extends his hands to push it away. Gets an inside edge and it drags down to deep fine leg..India vs Sri Lanka, 2nd Test Live Score: 263/8 (81.5 overs) 81.5: Prasidh Krishna to Lahiru Kumara, On a good length, on middle and leg. Kumara hops deep in the crease and backs away. Glides it behind point and the ball was close to hit the pad first..India vs Sri Lanka, 2nd Test Live Score: 263/8 (81.4 overs) 81.4: Prasidh Krishna to Sonal Dinusha, At 134.1 kph, on a back of a length. Sonal hobbles to the other end and seems to be experiencing cramps..India vs Sri Lanka, 2nd Test Live Score: 262/8 (81.3 overs) 81.3: Prasidh Krishna to Sonal Dinusha, Stays full, curving back in, on middle. Sonal knocks it through extra cover but does not take the single.

articles.title: Braves could be getting a dominant bullpen weapon back just in time
articles.summary: The Braves could be closing in on a major bullpen boost. Robert Suarez is nearing bullpen sessions, opening the door for the dominant reliever to return and...
articles.body:
Braves could be getting a dominant bullpen weapon back just in time originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here .

The Atlanta Braves could be getting one of their most effective relievers back before the end of the season.

Robert Suarez is expected to begin throwing bullpen sessions soon as he continues working his way back from right arm inflammation. While Atlanta has yet to establish a firm return date, Suarez's progress has kept open the possibility of a late-season return.

And based on what Suarez accomplished before going down, getting him back would be significant.

The 35-year-old has been dominant in his first season with Atlanta, posting a 4-0 record with a 0.56 ERA, four saves and 26 strikeouts across 31 appearances. Suarez has allowed just 21 hits and six walks over 32 innings, producing an impressive 0.84 WHIP.

He surrendered only two earned runs and one home run before landing on the injured list.

Braves get encouraging Robert Suarez news

Suarez hasn't pitched since June 19, when he worked 1⅓ scoreless innings against the Milwaukee Brewers . Atlanta initially described his issue as forearm soreness before placing him on the injured list with inflammation. An MRI provided encouraging news, showing no ligament damage or structural changes.

Now the focus is getting him back on a mound.

Bullpen sessions will provide Atlanta with a better indication of how close Suarez is to facing hitters. If he responds well, the next steps could include live batting practice and potentially a rehabilitation assignment before activation.

There is little reason for the Braves to rush the process.

Suarez's numbers demonstrate how valuable he can be when healthy. His ability to handle high-leverage innings provides another late-game option and could help shorten games down the stretch.

Before joining Atlanta, Suarez established himself as one of baseball's more reliable late-inning relievers with San Diego . He recorded 40 saves in 2025 and entered this season with extensive closing experience.

Atlanta doesn't necessarily need him to immediately resume a full workload.

If Suarez can return healthy and regain his command, even a limited role could strengthen the bullpen.

For now, his comeback remains a work in progress.

But after producing a 0.56 ERA through his first 31 appearances, Suarez has already shown what he can provide.

The Braves are hoping they'll get another opportunity to use it before the season ends.
